clue.text: For drying caparisons

parts.note: caparisons are ornamental cloths for a horse, so the clue reads as horse clothing, while the item meant is a frame for airing laundry

explanation.surface: Someone is hanging out the decorative cloths of a horse to dry.
explanation.walkthrough: Caparisons are a horse's clothes, so a 'horse' for 'clothes' to dry on is described literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden frame on which washing is hung to air is this, the clue's whimsical reading making it gear dressing a horse.

clue.text: Russian ship with a bird circling

indicators.note: circling says the bird's letters go round the ship and the a

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A Russian vessel is shown with a seabird flying round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossacks were horsemen of southern Russia, so the word serves as a nationality-flavoured noun for a Russian.

clue.text: She wrote in two languages? That's right!

parts.note: yes, agreeing, is oui in French
yes, agreeing, is da in Russian

explanation.surface: A bilingual author is confirmed with an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in two languages' tells you to say 'yes' twice, once in French and once in Russian. Ouida was the pen name of the Victorian novelist Maria Louise Ramé.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian novelist Maria Louise Ramé published under this pen name, so she is a woman who wrote.

clue.text: Over the man further up, we hear, in the grading system

annotationWithheld.why: Over the man further up, we hear, in the grading system (9): a homophone of 'higher' plus something for 'Archy', but no reading found that gives 'Over' and 'the man' each a job
annotationWithheld.clue: Over the man further up, we hear, in the grading system

clue.text: Bullet — it moves slowly

definitions.meaning: a bullet or lump of metal fired from a gun is a ... in slang
a slimy shell-less garden mollusc is proverbially slow

explanation.surface: A bullet is described as something sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: slang for a bullet and the name of a slow-crawling garden mollusc.

clue.text: Upset about act

parts.note: about, as in 'concerning', means over (talk over a matter)
an act on a stage bill is a turn

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed about a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as an adjective but is the verb, to knock over.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset something is to knock it over or capsize it, a synonym.

clue.text: Shandy's inventor, they say, is back

indicators.note: they say signals a word heard rather than read

parts.note: Laurence Sterne wrote the novel Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: The creator of a beer-and-lemonade drink is said to have returned.
explanation.walkthrough: Shandy looks like the drink; it is Tristram Shandy, the novel by Laurence Sterne.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear part of a ship is its stern, so it means back.

clue.text: Revenue officials unfortunately are rusty

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The tax collectors are sadly out of practice.
explanation.definitionFit: The government department handling public revenue and its officials is called this, a collective noun.

clue.text: From which captain directs the game

definitions.meaning: the raised platform from which a ship's captain gives orders
a card game for four players in pairs

explanation.surface: A team captain is giving orders on a game.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a ship's command platform and the four-handed card game descended from whist.

clue.text: Reused ill-treated calculator

indicators.note: treated, read with ill as mistreated, signals that these letters are handled roughly and rearranged

explanation.surface: A recycled calculator has been abused.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'ill-treated': 'ill' joins 'Reused' as fodder, and 'treated' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-electronic device of sliding logarithmic scales was used for arithmetic, so it is an early calculator.

clue.text: Terrorists who can give us the slip

indicators.note: who can give us says the word itself contains and yields the letters wanted

explanation.surface: Terrorists might escape their pursuers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give us the slip' reads as an escape, but 'slip' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, a synonym.

clue.text: Where vessel docked with two painters in the middle of Bath

indicators.note: in places the painters inside the central letters
the middle of takes the inner letters of the word Bath
two says the painter abbreviation is taken twice

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A boat moored where two artists were at work in the middle of the city of Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is the English city; 'the middle of' strips its first and last letters. Noah's ark is the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible says Noah's ark came to rest on the mountains of this name in Turkey.

clue.text: Flag, one way and another

parts.note: ST, street, is one kind of way
another way is a road, RD, so a road gives A plus RD

explanation.surface: A banner can be flown one way and the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner or ensign carried as an emblem.

clue.text: Hayricks not ever troubled in spirit

indicators.note: troubled suggests disturbance, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not removes the word for ever from the hay-ricks

parts.note: printed hay-ricks, stacks of hay
ay, poetic, means ever or always

explanation.surface: Haystacks never disturbed in spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove AY (ever) from HAYRICKS, then shuffle HRICKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirsch is a clear cherry brandy, a spirit.

clue.text: Close it up with new wrapping

indicators.note: wrapping says the word for new goes round the other piece

parts.note: recent means new

indicators.note: up in a down clue reads the word it upwards

explanation.surface: Seal it up with a fresh cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a verb but is the adjective, as in close-mouthed; 'up' turns 'it' in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone close is secretive and says little, a synonym.

clue.text: In the early stage, how creditors start to foreclose

indicators.note: In at the front places a letter inside the word for early stage

parts.note: a prelude is an opening stage

indicators.note: start takes the opening letter of creditors

explanation.surface: At first, creditors move to foreclose.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude is to rule out in advance, which is to foreclose a possibility.

clue.text: Yowl — provide a sound barrier!

parts.note: to cater is to provide food

indicators.note: sound signals the barrier word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a wall is a barrier

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks to set up soundproofing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound barrier' reads as an aircraft term; 'a sound barrier' is WAUL, heard like wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterwaul is a cat's wailing cry, a synonym for a yowl.

clue.text: Time to conceal where the fruit comes from

parts.note: a date is a point in time
to palm a coin is to conceal it in the hand

explanation.surface: A moment to hide the origin of the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree bearing dates is where that fruit grows.

clue.text: Sack in which sailors keep shanties?

definitions.text: Sack in which sailors keep shanties?

parts.words: Sack in which sailors keep shanties?
parts.note: shanties as songs suggests ditties, so a sailor's bag of odds and ends is jokily a bag for songs

explanation.surface: Seamen store their songs in a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors kept sewing kit and small belongings in a pouch of this name, and ditties are songs like shanties.

clue.text: Commit murder to get estate

annotationWithheld.why: Commit murder to get estate (6): printed so on the scan; DO IN for commit murder gives no MA and no other word supplies it

clue.text: Stopped being spoken of as sober

indicators.note: being spoken of signals a word heard rather than read

parts.note: staid means sober and sedate

explanation.surface: Someone stopped being called sober.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stopped somewhere is to have remained there, a synonym.

clue.text: Doctor, old to be right person to assist surgeon

parts.note: esse is the Latin infinitive to be, an old tongue

explanation.surface: A doctor is past it, the right one to help in theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser is a hospital assistant who dresses wounds for a surgeon.

clue.text: Me a clerk? Confound it, I'm a swimmer!

indicators.note: confound means to mix up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An indignant fish protests at being taken for an office worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A mackerel is a fish, a swimmer speaking in the first person.

clue.text: Heart-broken in a foxhole

indicators.note: broken suggests something smashed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken-hearted soldier in a foxhole.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox's burrow is called its earth.

clue.text: Miss Woodhouse rang back, wanting an insignificant weight

indicators.note: back reads the whole assembled string from end to start

parts.note: Emma Woodhouse is the heroine of Jane Austen's Emma

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letters of an are removed from rang

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Jane Austen's heroine phoned back, wanting a tiny weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' governs both pieces, so the whole string is read in reverse; 'wanting an' strips those two letters from 'rang'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramme is a tiny metric unit of mass, hence an insignificant weight.

clue.text: Bird may not complete bird call

indicators.note: not complete drops the final letter of may

parts.note: caw is the call of a crow

explanation.surface: A bird might not finish its call.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large parrot, a bird.

clue.text: 22 left in the island

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the island word

parts.note: a cay is a low island or reef

explanation.surface: Something is left on the island.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 refers to the answer to 22 Down, the soil found in a foxhole.
explanation.definitionFit: Clay is a kind of soil, the ground meaning of the cross-referenced answer.

clue.text: Victor drops first point in the ring

indicators.note: drops first removes the opening letter of the word for victor

parts.note: a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: A boxer loses an early point in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring is an archery target: the inner is the ring next to the bull, and a shot there scores.
explanation.definitionFit: On a target the circle just outside the bull is called the inner, a scoring zone.

clue.text: Unions — every one rises from forebears

parts.note: every one is all
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: from here means taken away from, so the hills are removed from the forebears

parts.note: forebears are ancestors
tors are rocky rises or hills

explanation.surface: Every trade union grows out of earlier ones.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove TORS (rises, hills) from ANCESTORS, leaving ANCES.
explanation.definitionFit: Alliances are unions formed between parties, a synonym.

clue.text: Ship following after them, always let down

indicators.note: after places the clue's following letter behind the word them, with always slipped in before it

parts.note: ay, poetic, means always
to lower is to let down

explanation.surface: A ship trails behind others, always lowered.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pilgrim Fathers' vessel of 1620 is one particular ship.
